description: Proving Ground talks from BSides Las Vegas 2026.

talks.title: Wednesday
talks.teaser: Covers four Proving Ground talks on IoT logs, npm supply chain attacks, cloud exposure scanning and AI bug hunting.
talks.summary:
This Proving Ground recording bundles four short talks, each addressing a different defensive problem. The first covers detecting attacks on air-gapped IoT devices. A proof-of-concept collects and normalizes device logs, groups them into templates, flags new or shifting patterns and volume spikes, then uses a small local language model to draft a summary for an analyst. The presenter acknowledged the setup consumes most of the device's CPU and memory, and that the model recommends actions rather than taking them.

The middle talks move to software supply chains and cloud exposure. One speaker walked through recent npm compromises, where malicious install scripts harvested developer credentials, and described a pipeline that watches newly published packages, runs open-source scanners, has AI triage the results, and pushes verdicts to a developer-side firewall with a minimum package age. A second speaker showed how to catch internet-exposed services within minutes by combining inventory snapshots and cloud change events with targeted port scans, instead of waiting for scheduled sweeps.

The final talk described an experiment that builds code graphs, slices paths from user input to sensitive sinks, and hands them to LLM agents that test a live WordPress plugin. It surfaced a blind SQL injection in a widely installed plugin, though it also produced many low-impact findings. The shared takeaways are to keep developer endpoints and untrusted inputs in scope, shorten the gap between a change and its verification, and keep AI output checkable with pass-or-fail tests.

talks.title: Tuesday
talks.teaser: Covers a full day of Proving Ground talks on crypto flaws, AI agent security, exploit development, and macOS malware.
talks.summary: This recording collects a full day of the Proving Ground stage at BSides Las Vegas 2026, a run of separate short talks rather than one presentation. Early sessions look at recurring missing checks in cryptographic code, such as unvalidated signature values and JWT algorithm confusion, and show how a simple missing check lets a forged token or signature pass verification in a practice banking and login setup. Other sessions describe a campaign that used search engine poisoning, fake GitHub repositories, and a blockchain-based command channel to deliver remote access malware aimed at system administrators. Further talks cover generating vulnerable training environments with AI agents, governing AI tools inside an educational publisher through a risk questionnaire and cross-team process, and a playbook for responding to prompt injection incidents in AI assistants. Later sessions cover probing voice AI agents with phone-based prompt injection, egress control for on-premises workloads and AI agents, securing Model Context Protocol servers, and the growth of macOS malware. A shellcode exploit against an old Windows web server under severe byte restrictions adds a deep technical example, while career advice and a historical talk on privacy and surveillance round out the day. Practitioners can take away concrete code checks, detection ideas, and governance patterns from across the sessions.
